To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel stochastic regulator for nonlinear systems affected by a nonlinear exosystem, and we show that the proposed regulator outperforms previous ones.

we provide a solution to a problem of nonlinear stochastic regulation with incomplete information, by using a Carleman embedding of the exosysten, that is a transformation that approximates the nonlinear exogenous system with an extended state that contains the state Kroneker powers up to a given order.

the Carleman method allows to solve a class of stochastic optimal regulator problems for bilinear systems with incomplete state information, where the exosystem state is not directly measurable and the state and the exosystem are affected by a nonlinear stochastic disturbance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a stochastic optimal regulator for a class of nonlinear systems, affected by additive and multiplicative state noises.
the problem of designing a state-feedback regulator for a class of nonlinear stochastic systems, affected by persistent disturbances provided by a nonlinear exosystem.
a class of nonlinear stochastic systems, affected by an exogenous system (drift and multiplicative noise).

, in the presence of a nonlinear exosystem, the Carleman technique is able to provide a solution of the stochastic optimal control in the incomplete information case, even though the solution is not unique.

, for this kind of systems, the optimal control is achieved through the Carleman approximation, which allows to obtain an optimal solution in the bilinear framework, and the regulator performances are significantly improved by increasing the order n of the approximation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a stochastic optimal regulator for a class of nonlinear systems, affected by nonlinear stochastic exogenous signals, with a bilinear approximation of the latter, and with incomplete information on both the system state and the exosystem state.
the Carleman approximation is a powerful technique to deal with nonlinear stochastic systems, which can be used in a wide range of applications.
the present work extends the results of [3] to the case of multiplicative noise and nonlinear drift.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Carleman method is a powerful tool to handle nonlinear stochastic systems with multiplicative state noise.
the Carleman method is able to deal with nonlinear stochastic systems in a way that is similar to what is done in the linear stochastic case.

the Carleman technique can be applied to solve optimal control problems for nonlinear stochastic systems with a persistent disturbance, provided that the nonlinear exogenous system is bilinear with respect to the extended state.
